title: ashley-martin-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-04
content:
On-call scratchpad - Ashley Martin (2026-03-04)

Summary for the shift:
- Quiet first half, spike in 02:15-02:45 UTC with a degraded Redis cluster causing elevated API latencies for hosted-api (region-us-west). Pages escalated to sev2, briefly hit customer-facing error rates (~0.8%).
- Main actions: failover promoted to replica, key eviction tuning reverted, restarted a misbehaving sidecar in the cache-proxy fleet.
- Follow-ups and runbook TODOs listed below.

Timeline / Notes:
- 02:12 UTC: Pager from monitoring (api-latency-alert) - p95 jumped from 210ms -> 720ms.
  - Initial checks: CPU fine on API nodes, error traces show timeouts to redis-master pool.
  - Slack: #sre-oncall pinged; opened JIRA-3421.
- 02:18 UTC: Confirmed redis-master had >95% client connections in BLOCKED state (threaded-io stalls).
  - Tried soft-restart (SIGTERM) on a proxy sidecar (cache-proxy-3); logs showed repeated OOMs on sidecar process.
- 02:25 UTC: Promoted replica (redis-replica-07) to master following runbook steps, slowly reattached replicas.
  - Observed latency improve over 5 minutes.
- 02:36 UTC: Error rate back to baseline. Post-incident monitoring stable.

Immediate follow-up (must do within 24-72h):
- JIRA-3421: Root cause analysis (assigned to @ethan) - suspected memory leak in cache-proxy sidecar after last deploy (2026-03-02). Add memory metrics to container dashboard (ALERT if RSS > 700MB for 5m).
- JIRA-3470: Load test for redis failover recovery time (assigned to @mia) - validate target failover <90s under typical traffic.
- Patch & rollback checklist: create a small canary to validate sidecar binary v1.2.4 -> v1.2.5; currently flagged in kanban under infra.

Runbook gaps / TODOs (my notes):
- Runbook step 3 (validate client draining) ambiguous when using sticky connections; update step to include commands to rotate upstream connections and check STATS via redis-cli.
- Add explicit troubleshooting snippet for detecting sidecar OOM vs OOMKilled (container vs process) - I had to grep logs manually.
- Add dashboard tile for sidecar RSS distribution across hosts (not just pod-level), and alert when >30% hosts exceed threshold.

Outstanding tasks (personal TODOs):
- Today (within shift):
  - Draft short incident blurb for ops-incident digest (2-3 bullets) - aim to post before EOD PST.
  - Open small PR to runbook: clarify connection draining commands and add example redis-cli INFO output. (PR branch: runbook/redis-failover-fixes)
  - Add memory alert to infra-alerts (link to alert rule in JIRA-3421).
- Follow-up this week:
  - Pair with infra team to reproduce sidecar leak in staging; schedule 1-hour sesh with @sam (SRE) and @liam (infra) next Tue.
  - End-to-end chaos test: simulate redis-master latency while ensuring fallback paths trigger correctly. Add to chaos-week backlog.

Notes / quick commands used:
- kubectl logs -n infra cache-proxy-3 | grep "OOM"
- redis-cli -h <ip> INFO memory | egrep "used_memory_human|maxmemory"
- git checkout -b runbook/redis-failover-fixes && edit runbook

Misc observations / ideas:
- Consider enabling per-tenant circuit-breaker for heavy cached endpoints; would limit blast radius on cache failure.
- Investigate scheduler placement: several cache-proxy instances were colocated on old host class (m5a) - consider draining and moving to newer m6i to avoid memory fragmentation.

Slack / comms to send:
- Short post to #ops-incident: 1) timeline 2) mitigation 3) next steps (RCA assigned). Draft: "02:12 UTC - transient Redis master stalls caused p95 latency spike; failover to replica resolved service. RCA tracked in JIRA-3421. Oncall: Ashley Martin. Follow-ups: memory alert + runbook updates."

Anything I missed? Quick checklist before sign-off:
- [ ] Post digest note in #ops-incident
- [ ] Create PR for runbook clarifications
- [ ] Add memory alert rule + link it in JIRA-3421
- [ ] Schedule pairing session for reproducing memory leak

End of scratchpad.
plain_text_preview: On-call scratchpad (Ashley Martin) - incident at 02:12 UTC; redis master stalls -> failover; follow-ups: JIRA-3421 (RCA), add memory alert, runbook updates.
